content: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Similarly, erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole through the same mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate reduces the levels or effects of oral forms of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The lumateperone dose should be reduced to 21 mg/day when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases lurasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The manufacturer recommends reducing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Concurrent use may increase the risk of lurasidone-related adverse effects. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels or effects of mavorizafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Adverse effects of mavorizafor should be monitored if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and mavorizafor prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring.
